The next-nearest-neighbor coupling J2 enhances ferromagnetic order and shifts the quantum critical point to h_c > 1.0 compared to the pure nearest-neighbor TFIM. Sweep h/J1 from 0.10 to 3.00 in steps of 0.05 (39 parameter points). Use the susceptibility peak and Binder cumulant to locate h_c. Additionally, repeat the full sweep for J2 = 0 and J2 = 0.5 (keeping J1 = 1 fixed) and demonstrate quantitatively how the critical point shifts upward as J2 increases. The NNN term introduces longer-range entanglement into the ground state, requiring deeper quantum circuits for accurate state preparation; quantify the additional circuit depth compared to the J2 = 0 case.
